references.text: Delilah asks Samson the same question for the first time: 'Tell me where your great strength comes from, and how you can be bound and subdued.'
Delilah accuses Samson of lying to her and asks again how he can be bound, following the same pattern as in verse 13.
Delilah accuses Samson once more of deception with similar wording: 'How can you say you love me when your heart is not with me?'
Delilah's weaving of Samson's hair is mentioned again when she actually cuts his seven locks, which are the source of his strength.
The Nazirite vow included that no razor should come upon the head, which explains the significance of Samson's hair and locks.
An earlier example of a woman pressuring Samson to reveal a secret through persistent persuasion.
